acceptance_criteria: parse_request({using:[], methodCalls:[...]}) returns Ok(JmapRequest); existing conformance test error-empty-using passes; no other parse_request tests regress
close_reason: removed empty-using guard from parse_request; renamed test to parse_request_empty_using_is_ok; fixed pre-existing broken doc links in lib.rs
description: parse_request currently rejects an empty using array with notRequest (HTTP 400). The RFC expert ruling in rfc-clarifications.md Q4 is: the server should process the request but return unknownMethod for every method call, because the client has not opted in to any capabilities. This is a conformance bug — the jmap-test-suite conformance test error-empty-using specifically checks for this behavior.
design:
Fix in crate-jmap-server/src/parse.rs:
1. Remove the using.is_empty() → notRequest guard from parse_request.
2. Update (or delete and replace) the parse_request_empty_using_is_error test — it currently asserts notRequest, which is wrong. New test: parse with empty using succeeds (Ok), then confirm the dispatcher returns unknownMethod for every method call in that request.
3. The dispatcher already returns unknownMethod for unregistered methods. For the conformance test (Core/echo, which is not registered), this is sufficient.
4. Longer-term: the dispatcher should enforce that a method's required capability URI is present in using before executing it. That is a separate, larger issue — file it as a follow-on. For now, removing the blanket 400 is the minimum correct fix.

Ref: rfc-clarifications.md Q4; jmap-test-suite src/tests/core/request-errors.test.ts id=error-empty-using.
title: jmap-server: empty using[] must yield unknownMethod per call, not notRequest
